Hi Tamara,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — really appreciated the candid breakdown of FinEdge's priorities. Below is a short recap to make sure we're aligned and to capture next steps. If anything is off, flag it and we'll update.

Summary of pain points (as we heard it)
- Token/unit economics: current LLM costs are chewing into margins for batch scoring workflows (esp. reconciliation jobs).
- Latency SLAs: some pipelines need sub-200ms tail latency for user-facing flows; others are batch/async and can tolerate higher latency.
- Ops friction: internal infra team wants predictable throughput and easier autoscaling rather than hand-tuning GPU fleets.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Inference: in-house model endpoints on mixed GPU fleet (mostly T4s + a few A10s) managed by ops team.
- Serving layer: a mix of custom REST endpoints and a Kafka-backed async pipeline for overnight scoring.
- Observability: basic Prometheus metrics, but no token-level cost visibility or per-route latency breakdowns.

Success criteria for a pilot
- Unit cost reduction: meaningful per-token reduction for batch scoring (target: 20–35% cheaper than today).
- Latency preservation: keep latency for user-facing routes within 200–300ms p95.
- Ops integration: show a non-disruptive deployment path (no hot re-architecting of their pipelines) and clear autoscaling behavior.

Technical openness
- Quantization: FinEdge engineering indicated willingness to test int8/q4-lite variants for batch jobs but only after validating output fidelity on a small subset.
- Batching/caching: strong interest in prefix/KV caching for chat-like routes and continuous batching for batch scoring.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) We'll share a short pilot-scope doc (attached) that outlines workloads, target KPIs, and data transfer assumptions.
2) You mentioned two representative workload traces — could you send the CSV with sample calls and token distributions (we marked this as "workload-samples.csv").
3) If procurement needs to be looped in, please share contact details (email accepted) and we can provide an indicative cost estimate for a 6-week pilot.
4) Proposed follow-up: 30m tech sync next Tue (8/24) to align on pilot traces and scheduling.

Attachments: pilot-scope.pdf (pilot objectives, metrics, rough timeline)

Thanks — will be on standby to pull in SE resources.

Best,

Thanks Michael — this looks right from our perspective. A few clarifications and asks: 

- On unit-cost: we measured current batch scoring unit cost at roughly $0.012 per 1k tokens (varies by model). Our goal is to get under $0.009 for the night-time scoring window without impacting quality.
- Latency note: the p95 < 200ms target is only for the fraud-detect realtime endpoint. All other endpoints can accept up to 1s p95.
- Quantization: our ML team is OK with an initial fidelity evaluation on a holdout of 1% of requests. If the delta is <1% on the reconciliation metric we use, they are comfortable proceeding.

Procurement: please send any standard pilot paperwork to procurement@finedge.com — they will handle the PO if we get alignment.

I can get the workload CSV over by EOD Monday. Also, curious: do you provide any upfront ballpark on expected cost delta (rough estimate) before we sign? We just need a sense so procurement can prioritize.
